 Judgment

Municipal Corporation Of Delhi ......... Complainant Versus M/S Apollo Pharmacy
through its Ar Mr.Jayvardhan Binjola Shop No.D-82, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi.
.............. Accused Offence punishable u
nder Section - 417 read with Section - 416 of The Delhi Municipal Corporation Act,1957 1.

By way of the present Judgment, this court shall dispose off challan bearing No. 271/2024, of Apollo Pharmacy located at shop no. D-82, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi dated 05.02.2024 against Mr.
Jayvardhan Binjola (Authorised Representative of Apollo pharmacy), under section-417 of Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 (hereinafter referred to as "DMC Act").
BRIEF FACTS:
2.

It is alleged against the accused that the pharmacy shop namely, Apollo Pharmacy located at shop no. D-82, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi dated 05.02.24 was found being running without a valid MCD Health Trade License (HTL) within the jurisdiction of South district in contravention of DMC Act,
thereby accused has committed the offence punishable under section-417 read with section-461 of DMC Act.
3.
It is pertinent to mention here that the cognizance of the offence had already been taken by this court on 21.02.2024 and a fine was proposed for the summary disposal of the case under the DMC Act.
The Authorised Representative (AR) of the accused exercised the option to contest the present challan and accordingly the same is being taken up for adjudication as per law.

PROCEEDINGS BEFORE THE COURT:
Mcd vs M/S Apollo Pharmacies-46510 on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117616575/
1 4.

sentences.text: The accused entered his first appearance on 21.02.2024.
Notice under section-251 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) was framed against the accused on the same day, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
It was the defence of the accused that the shop trade in pharmaceutical items and is being run, after taking a valid licence from the Drug Control Department as per the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.
Therefore, no licence from MCD is required to run the said pharmaceutical shop and he is not liable to pay any fine for not having any license under the DMC Act.
5. Summons were issued to the relevant officer on behalf of the MCD South Branch, and Public Health Inspector entered appearance before this court who was examined by this court as PW-1.
The witness PW-1 placed on record few photographs of the shop in question as Ex.PW1/C and circular no.PA/MHO-I/MCD/2022/97 dated 07.07.2022 as Ex.PW1/B with respect to the present challan.
Opportunity was granted to cross examine PW1 and the same was cross examined by the counsel for the accused.

6. After cross-examination the prosecution closed its evidence and then statement of the AR of the accused under section-313 of Cr.P.C was recorded, wherein he denied all the incriminating evidence and the allegations of the prosecution.

He stated that the shop in question is being run by the company i.e., M/S Apollo Pharmacies Ltd after obtaining a valid license from the Drug Control Department under Drugs and cosmetics Act, 1940 and from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI).

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He further stated that no HTL is required to run the shop in question from the MCD thus, he has no liability in the present challan.
Further, he chose not to lead any defence evidence to that effect.
APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE LED BEFORE THIS COURT:
7. To I have heard the arguments advanced by the parties as well as the materials placed on record before this court.

8. Before delving into the facts placed before this court, it is necessary to reiterate the legal provisions. Section-417 of the DMC Act, 1957 states as follows:
417.Premises not to be used for certain purposes without licence (1) No person shall use or permit to be used any premises for any of the following purposes without or otherwise than in conformity with the terms of a licence granted by the Commissioner in this behalf namely:
(a) any of the purposes specified in Part I of the Eleventh Schedule;
(b) any purpose which is, in the opinion of the Commissioner dangerous to life,
health or property or likely to create a nuisance,
(c) keeping horses.

entities.text: Part I of the Eleventh Schedule
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text:
cattle or other quadruped animals or birds for transportation, sale or hire or for sale of the produce thereof: or Mcd vs M/S Apollo Pharmacies-46510 on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117616575/
2 (d) storing any of the articles specified in Part II of the Eleventh Schedule except for domestic use of any of those articles:
Provided that the corporation may declare that premises in which the aggregate quantity of articles stored for sale does not exceed such quantity as may be prescribed by bye-laws in respect of any such articles shall be exempted from the operation of clause (d).

entities.text: Mcd vs M/S Apollo Pharmacies-46510 on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ( 2) In prescribing the terms of a licence granted under this section for the use of premises as mills or iron yards or for similar purposes the Commissioner may.
when he thinks fit, require the licensee to provide a space or passage within the premises for carts for loading and unloading purposes.
(3) The Corporation shall fix a scale of fees to be paid in respect of premises licensed under sub-section (1).
9. Coming to the present MCD challan, as per the statement of PW-1 the name of the shop is Apollo Pharmacy and the employee of the accused found at the shop had signed the challan.
The prosecution had examined PW-1 and it had precipitated from his testimony that challan Ex.PW1/A is generated by him.
PW-1 stated that apart from medicines, the accused was also selling other grocery items like baby food products and other food products as shown in Ex.PW1/C.
In his testimony PW-1 testified that the employee of the accused namely Mr. Nihaluddin at the shop signed the challan Ex.PW1/A.
PW-1 had denied all the suggestions put to him regarding absence of violation of DMC Act and non-requirement of the shop to get license from the MCD.

10. The counsel for the accused submitted that the shop in question is a pharmacy shop and is engaged in trade of pharmaceutical products apart from small quantity of cosmetics as well as baby food products.
The counsel for the accused further stated that the shop is being run after taking a valid license from the Drug Control Department under the Drugs and Cosmetics act as well as from FSSAI.

The counsel argued that as per Section-417 of DMC Act the accused is not required to get any license from the MCD since the pharmaceutical items falls under item-21 of the Eleven Schedule,
which does not mentions sale or trade as one of the necessary criteria for obtaining licence.

The second argument of the accused is that as per the proviso of section-417 the accused is given liberty to sell small quantity of cosmetics and food products thus, the provisions of the said section have not been violated by the accused person.

The counsel for the accused has relied on a judgment pronounced by this court titled as SDMC vs M/S Apollo Hospital Enterprises Ltd. MCD Challan No.
36580 dated 22.08.2015 in support of his arguments.
11.

entities.text:
SDMC vs M/S Apollo Hospital Enterprises Ltd. MCD Challan No.
36580
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A bare reading of Section-417 along with Eleventh Schedule shows that as per section-417(1)(a)
premises cannot be used without obtaining a valid licence from the Commissioner of MCD for any of the purposes mentioned in Part-1 of the Eleventh Schedule.

It is a well settled law that the entries in the Eleventh Schedule are in the nature of restraint on the trade by regulating and stipulating a requirement of license therefore, are to be interpreted in a restrictive manner.
The scope of each entries in the Schedule cannot be expanded by employing aids or explanations to it.

The issue whether trade of all the purposes mentioned in entry-21 in the Part-1 of the Eleventh Schedule is prohibited or not without obtaining a valid license from the Commissioner was discussed by the Mcd vs M/S Apollo Pharmacies-46510 on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117616575/
3 Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Sumitra Devi Malik vs MCD & Anr. 1998 (47) DRJ 19.

entities.text: Mcd vs M/S Apollo Pharmacies-46510 on
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sumitra Devi Malik vs MCD & Anr. 1998 (47) DRJ 19
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraph is being reproduced as follows:
"A perusal of entry No.21 also shows that it is only manufacturing, packing, pressing and the processing in respect of the articles, which is prohibited without licence and not the trading in the items.

Accordingly, there is no merit in the contention of the appellant that the respondent is prohibited from carrying on trade in acrylic,
kashmilon wool, silk yarn and hand-knitted yarns etc."

12. In view of above settled law, this court is of the opinion that there is merit in the argument of the accused and the accused does not require any license for 'trade' of pharmaceutical or medical products from his shop in question.
13. Now coming to the other argument of the accused that the shop of the accused can trade in cosmetics and baby food products, in small quantity as per the proviso to Section-417 of the DMC Act.
It is clear from bare perusal of the Section-417 that the permission of the Commissioner of the MCD is required for trade, storage and health purposes.

While the Commissioner may issue 'General Trade License' for all the purposes mention in Part-1 and 'Storage license' for those in Part-2 of the Eleventh Schedule as per section-417(1)(a) and (d) respectively.
It also has power to issue license to restrain certain activities so to prevent nuisance on account of it being dangerous to life, health and property under section-417(1)(b).
And for all this purpose the Commissioner has been given explicit power under Section-417(3) to fix fees to be paid in respect of premises licensed under sub-section (1).

The Hon'ble Delhi High Court in M/S North Eastern Carrying Corporation vs Municipal Corporation of Delhi W.P(C) No. 5294/1999 decided on 20.04.2010 had observed that "sub-section (3) of Section-417 of DMC Act, 1957 is wholly independent part of Section-417 and even on assuming the requirement of payment of license fee is illegal, the same will not mean that the requirement of a licence also is automatically done away with."
14.

entities.text: M/S North Eastern Carrying Corporation vs Municipal Corporation of Delhi W.P(C) No. 5294/1999
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, although the shop in question is primarily trading in pharmaceutical or medicinal products but it is also dealing in grocery items like chocolates, shampoo, hair oil among others which can be clearly shown from Ex.PW1/B filed by the prosecution.
There is also PW1/D which goes on to show that these items are being sold by the accused from its shop in question.

The Commissioner of the MCD, in exercise of its power under Section-417(3) had issued circular Ex.PW1/C in which fees for both "Kiryana goods" at serial no. 50 and "Sale of Pharmaceuticals or Chemist Shop" at serial no. 55 has been prescribed.
Although, no 'licence for trade' is required for trade of pharmaceutical products only, strictly speaking as discussed in the foregoing paragraphs.

But harmonious interpretation of Ex.PW1/B with section-417(1)(a), shows that Ex.PW1/B has been issued to deal with such shops where miscellaneous products are being sold in addition to the pharmaceuticals or medical products.

The argument that the accused is selling such grocery products in small quantity, if accepted will lead to unwarranted instances where the grocery/kirana shops will start selling medicines or pharmaceutical products in small quantity and will argue similarly to evade obtaining license from the MCD.
Further, the argument that the accused can sell small quantity of baby food products or grocery items in view of proviso to Section-417(1) is also not tenable and the same is being misinterpreted.

As the proviso gives the discretion to the Mcd vs M/S Apollo Pharmacies-46510 on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117616575/
4 Commissioner to limit the aggregate quantity of articles stores for sale, which is not the case at hand.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the prosecution has successfully discharged its burden and the accused shop is found doing trade without having a valid licence issued by the MCD.

Merely by obtaining license from the Drug Control Department under the Drugs and Cosmetic Act, 1940 and from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) will not absolve the accused from obtaining license from the MCD under relevant category.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
15. Regarding the judgment relied upon by the counsel for the accused, indubitably with regard to the proposition of law laid down in the said judgment i.e., SDMC vs M/S Apollo Hospital Enterprises Ltd. MCD Challan No. 36580 dated 22.08.2015 but the same is not applicable to the facts of the present case as the said judgment dealt with trade of cosmetics products only and not grocery items.
16.

entities.text: SDMC vs M/S Apollo Hospital Enterprises Ltd. MCD Challan No. 36580
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Based on the preceding settled position of law along with all the facts and circumstances, this court has arrived at the conclusion that the prosecution has been successful to prove their case beyond reasonable doubt.
VERDICT 17.
Accordingly, accused M/s Apollo Pharmacy is hereby convicted for offence punishable under Section 417 read with Section 461 of the DMC Act.
18. Let the convict be heard separately on quantum of sentence.
Copy of this judgment be given free of cost to the convict.
Announced in the Open Court on this 4th June 2024.
